security_audit.summary: Most findings are scanner false positives caused by Markdown backticks, CSS borders, JavaScript template literals, loopback networking, and ordinary key enumeration. Confirmed risks include unsandboxed nested Claude execution, inherited secrets, forced port termination, browser injection paths, unsafe symlink handling, and shared temporary files. Publication should wait until high-impact execution, XSS, and file disclosure issues are fixed.

remediation.issue: Nested Claude processes receive untrusted prompts, broad tool access, and inherited environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Disable tools for trigger tests, allowlist required tools for rewriting, use a clean environment, and isolate execution from sensitive projects.

remediation.issue: Generated review pages insert untrusted data into script and HTML contexts.
remediation.suggestion: Escape less-than characters in embedded JSON, encode every placeholder for its context, sanitize SheetJS output, and add a restrictive content security policy.

remediation.issue: Viewer and packaging code can follow symlinks outside selected roots.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks, resolve every candidate path, and require each resolved path to remain below the approved workspace or skill directory.

remediation.issue: The review server terminates any process using the selected port.
remediation.suggestion: Do not kill existing listeners. Report the conflict or bind an automatically selected free loopback port.

remediation.issue: Skill names and shell placeholders are not constrained before path or command use.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names as slugs, construct subprocess arguments as arrays, and quote every path in documented shell commands.

remediation.issue: Temporary files and staging directories use predictable shared paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use exclusive temporary files and private temporary directories, then remove them with guaranteed cleanup.

remediation.issue: Grader agents treat generated artifacts as ordinary instructions.
remediation.suggestion: State that transcripts and outputs are untrusted evidence, forbid following embedded commands, and restrict grader tools to required reads and writes.

remediation.issue: Generated pages load remote fonts and a third-party script.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required assets locally or obtain explicit consent for external requests. Keep integrity metadata and pin exact versions.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Content Reaches Tool-Capable Nested Agents
semantic_findings.description: Skill content and raw evaluation queries are sent to Claude CLI without an explicit tool denylist. Prompt injection can influence nested agent actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both paths directly interpolate untrusted text and launch Claude CLI. Neither command constrains tools or supplies a minimal environment.

semantic_findings.title: Embedded Review Data Can Break Out of Script Context
semantic_findings.description: Serialized run data is inserted directly into a script element. Output containing a closing script tag can inject active HTML or JavaScript.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: json.dumps does not escape the HTML closing-script sequence. The resulting string is inserted verbatim inside the template's script element.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Template Placeholders Permit HTML Injection
semantic_findings.description: The workflow replaces skill name, description, and evaluation data placeholders without requiring HTML or script-context escaping.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The placeholders occupy raw HTML and JavaScript contexts, while the replacement instructions require direct substitution and specify no escaping.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink Following Can Disclose Files
semantic_findings.description: Viewer generation and packaging follow files found below user-selected directories. Symlinks can include files outside the intended workspace or skill root.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file and the subsequent read or archive operation follow symlinks. No resolved-path containment check rejects targets outside the selected root.

semantic_findings.title: Skill Name Is Used in a Filesystem Path Without Validation
semantic_findings.description: A skill name from frontmatter becomes part of a command filename. Path separators can escape the intended commands directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The name is concatenated into a Path without a slug check or basename normalization. The file is later written and unlinked.

semantic_findings.title: Evaluation Artifacts Are Not Marked as Untrusted Data
semantic_findings.description: The grader reads transcripts and output files without instructions to ignore embedded commands. Adversarial outputs can manipulate grading or request unrelated tool actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The grader is explicitly directed to read arbitrary artifacts but receives no prompt-injection boundary. Exploitability depends on the hosting agent's tool permissions.

high_findings.title: Python subprocess.run
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The subprocess runs lsof, then line 298 terminates every returned PID for the selected port. A user-selected port can therefore stop an unrelated local service without confirmation.

content.value_statement: Skill development often lacks repeatable testing and evidence. This skill guides drafting, evaluation, benchmarking, revision, trigger optimization, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Drafts new skill instructions from user goals, workflows, dependencies, and expected outputs.
Revises existing skills using user feedback, transcripts, and repeated evaluation results.
Creates realistic positive and negative trigger queries for description testing.
Aggregates graded runs into benchmark summaries with pass rates, timing, and token statistics.
Generates browser review pages for outputs, grades, benchmarks, and user feedback.
Validates and packages a skill directory as a distributable skill archive.
limitations: Description optimization requires an installed and authenticated Claude CLI.
Parallel comparisons require subagent support, while browser review requires a display or static HTML access.
Evaluation quality depends on representative prompts, objective assertions, and careful human review.
Included scripts create files, invoke local commands, and may start a local server.

use_cases.title: Create a First Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeatable workflow into structured instructions, supporting resources, and practical test prompts.
use_cases.target_user: Developers creating their first reusable AI skill

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Compare revised and baseline outputs, review failures, and refine instructions across measured iterations.
use_cases.target_user: Skill maintainers improving reliability and output quality

use_cases.title: Optimize Skill Triggering
use_cases.description: Test positive and negative queries, measure trigger rates, and select a stronger description using held-out results.
use_cases.target_user: AI platform teams managing large skill catalogs

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [workflow]. Ask about inputs, outputs, tools, edge cases, and triggering phrases before drafting it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new skill from a clear workflow idea.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Identify unclear instructions, missing safeguards, weak trigger guidance, and opportunities for progressive disclosure.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a skill without running a full evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Run Comparative Evaluations
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the skill at [path] using [test prompts]. Compare revised and baseline outputs, grade assertions, and summarize benchmark results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Measure whether a revision improves behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize the trigger description for [skill path] using positive and negative queries, validate held-out performance, then package the approved version.
prompt_templates.scenario: Complete an advanced release workflow with trigger testing.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that converts interview notes into structured research summaries.
output_examples.output: A skill draft with trigger guidance, a focused workflow, expected output sections, edge-case handling, and three realistic evaluation prompts.

output_examples.input: Compare my revised spreadsheet skill against its original version.
output: A benchmark summary comparing pass rate, execution time, and token use.
A review page showing both output sets, formal grades, and feedback controls.
Revision recommendations tied to repeated failures and transcript evidence.

output_examples.input: Improve when my deployment skill activates, without causing unrelated triggers.
output_examples.output: A balanced trigger test set, measured train and holdout results, and a concise description selected from evaluated alternatives.

best_practices: Confirm the intended workflow, trigger conditions, inputs, outputs, and dependencies before drafting.
Use realistic prompts and assertions that verify meaningful outcomes instead of file presence alone.
Review qualitative outputs with the user before applying benchmark-driven revisions.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize against a small test set without separate holdout queries.
Do not treat high pass rates as sufficient when assertions are weak or non-discriminating.
Do not package third-party skill directories before reviewing scripts, links, symlinks, and generated files.

faq.question: Can this skill create a skill from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers requirements, drafts instructions, proposes tests, supports evaluation, and packages the completed skill.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preserve a baseline, compare outputs, analyze feedback, and revise the skill across multiple iterations.

faq.question: Does it require the Claude CLI?
faq.answer: Only automated description optimization requires Claude CLI. Drafting, review, validation, and packaging can use other supported environments.

faq.question: Does it support Codex?
faq.answer: The guidance supports Codex, but Claude-specific optimization scripts require Claude CLI and its authentication.

faq.question: How are skill improvements measured?
faq.answer: The workflow combines assertion pass rates, repeated-run variance, time, token use, transcript analysis, and human feedback.

faq.question: Can it package the final skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The included validator checks basic structure, and the packager creates a distributable skill archive.
